correspondence.interval: Western initial headwater southeast of Lepaterique
correspondence.finding: The selected southeastward upper corridor matches the watercourse labeled Río San José on the Lepaterique sheet. It belongs to the western approach to Grande, rather than the Guacerique route farther north. The receiving name Choluteca is not extended over this headwater label.

correspondence.interval: Southern bend and eastward connection toward Concepción and Grande
correspondence.finding: The upper connector follows the northern edge of the Ojojona sheet through the San Sebastián-labeled valley and onward to the Grande corridor at Concepción de Río Grande. San Buenaventura directly labels Río Grande on the eastward reach that turns north toward Tegucigalpa. These historical sheets and JICA's later upper-basin map resolve the selected connection without naming it all Choluteca.

correspondence.interval: Tegucigalpa, northern loop, eastern turn and southbound middle valley
correspondence.finding: The complete distinctive route agrees with JICA Figure F.1.2: the receiving river runs north from Tegucigalpa, bends east and then south. Figure F.1.1 separately distinguishes Grande, Guacerique, San José and Chiquito approaches, so the selected modeled mainstem is not treated as evidence that all those waterways share one name.

correspondence.interval: Lower southwestward course and coastal terminal approach
correspondence.finding: JICA's whole-basin map supports the continuation southwest through the lower Choluteca corridor to the Gulf of Fonseca. On the detailed Punta Condega sheet, the selected terminal setting follows Río Choluteca into the Estero La Joya corridor toward Estero El Pedregal. The latter labels describe estuarine components, not alternative names for the entire river.

The actual southern beginning lies on the directly labeled Driftwood Creek corridor. It runs north through the mountain valley and turns northwest past the separately mapped Kietag, Nucleus and Elbow creek approaches. The selected route remains on Driftwood rather than those arriving branches; the farthest formal source point is not asserted.

Driftwood continues northwest and then west into the Utukok River. The separately named upper Utukok approaches from the south near Adventure Creek and is shown beginning farther upstream at the Kogruk/Tupik setting; that southern main-river continuation is not the chosen model headwater. The model follows the eastern Driftwood approach before joining the common receiving trunk.

The selected Utukok receiving reach runs north past the Seismo Creek vicinity, makes the broad eastward foothill bend, then turns north near the Carbon Creek and Ketik River surroundings. Repeated Utukok labels identify this irregular course. The nearby Colville drainage to the east and Kokolik/Avingak drainage to the west are separate.

Across the middle coastal plain, the selected trunk bends west and northwest below the Ilakoluk vicinity and continues on the repeatedly labeled Utukok. The Avak and Ivisaruk corridors farther north and east are not substituted for it, and the selection does not traverse their named lakes or inlets.

The lower Utukok enters a broad marsh-fringed braided/delta setting on the Kasegaluk Lagoon mainland shore. The terminal enlargement distinguishes the labeled river, tidal-flat channels, lagoon and offshore barrier islands. The selected ending is retained as the delta/lagoon-margin transition, without assigning a precise active mouth arm, a present shoreline vertex or a river route through the lagoon to the sea.

The headward selection is in the valley southwest of Monsenhor Tabosa and east of Serra da Lagoa. The detailed municipal map prints Riacho Acaraú on this descending valley and Rio Acaraú farther south near Saco do Souza/Sítio do Souza. Riacho da Serra and Riacho do Mulungu are separately labeled adjoining branches. The modeled beginning is not promoted to an officially surveyed river source.

The southern bow passes the Chupador and Morro Redondo setting, turns west through the Cacimba dos Mocós area, then northwest past the Acaraú-labeled corridor toward Tamboril. The detailed maps distinguish Riacho do Gavião and Riacho do Salobro from the receiving route, and separate the Quixeramobim drainage east of the divide.

Around Tamboril, the west/northwestward continuation bears the local Riacho Fundo label. It continues through the Barra/Carnaúba direction toward Irapuá and the river directly labeled Rio Acaraú east of Nova Russas. The municipal sheet also distinguishes the nearby Riacho do Combe and Riacho da Carnaúba labels; exact local name-boundary vertices are not inferred. The more westerly Riacho do Curtume/Riacho do Feijão corridor through the Nova Russas urban setting is not substituted for the selected eastern receiving route.

Northward from the Nova Russas vicinity, the route passes Conceição and Recanto, follows the directly labeled Rio Acaraú west of Hidrolândia, and enters the southern arm of Açude Público Araras. It leaves the reservoir in the Varjota/Macaraú direction on the river again labeled Rio Acaraú. Rio Feitosa and Rio dos Macacos occupy separate eastern approaches; the reservoir remains a reservoir, not an alternate river name.

Below Araras the selected receiving river runs north through the Cariré–Groaíras surroundings to Sobral. Jacurutu and Groaíras approach from the east, while Jaibaras and Açude Aires de Souza are on the separate western branch. The selection follows the main receiving corridor, not one of those tributaries or their reservoirs.

The lower route passes Sobral and Santana do Acaraú, runs through the Morrinhos/Marco river plain, continues east of Bela Cruz and by Cruz, and reaches the estuarine channel north of Acaraú. The state map repeatedly names this connected river Rio Acaraú and depicts its Atlantic coastal opening. The generalized endpoint is retained as the estuarine/mouth setting rather than an exact shoreline crossing or present-day tidal-channel survey.

The upper modeled route approaches the Rio do Peixe valley near Vitória da Conquista, then reaches separately named Rio Turiaçu and continues northeast across Alto Turiaçu, the northwest corner of Zé Doca and the southern Santa Luzia do Paruá sheet. The initial southwestern approach before the mapped Rio do Peixe corridor is not continuously traced and remains material pending; no hydronym is assigned to that unresolved interval.

The receiving modeled mainstem follows the Rio Turiaçu corridor from the Araguatins/Turi Velho area toward the northbound lowland course west of the Presidente Sarney setting. The two detailed map coverages distinguish neighboring tributaries and continue the same receiving channel.

The mainstem crosses the Turiaçu lowland channel and floodplain-waterbody setting, receives the western Paruá branch, passes Santa Helena and Turilândia and reaches the broader lower channel toward Serrano do Maranhão and Bacuri. The map labels Turiaçu on the receiving course.

The terminal fragment follows the broad, explicitly labelled Rio Turiaçu estuarine channel and its westward/northward bend. Its modeled endpoint is upstream of Turiaçu town and of the continuation to the wider coastal bay; it is not the open-Atlantic mouth.

The actual separate western branch corresponds to Rio Paruá near Parnação/Guarirama, then through the São Bento and Machado–Guaribas setting to the Turiaçu receiving course. It is not another Turiaçu mainstem fragment.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
